turns.t: Hiya. I'm not really poorly or owt, it's just that the lady at the hospital said I should ask about my jabs.
Right, that's a sensible thing to ask. Which jabs did she have in mind, do you know? ~
She said something about pneumonia and the flu one. And something for shingles, but I wasn't listening properly, to be honest. ~
No bother, that's what I'm here for. Tell me first, how have you been lately, in yourself? ~
Champion, really. Better than I've been for a year or so. ~
Lovely. Have you had a temperature, or any cough, over the last few weeks?
No, nothing like that. No cough, no temperature.
And any infections that took a long time to shift, chest, water works, anything?
No, not since last winter. Nothing lately, thankfully.
Good. I've got your notes here, so remind me about your long-term health.
I've got lupus, they found it a few years back, and my kidneys aren't brilliant, chronic kidney disease they call it.
That's what I've got written, thank you. Do you smoke or drink at all?
I don't drink, not for years now. Never been a smoker, either.
Do you have any allergies, to medicines, foods, anything that's ever given you trouble?
No. Not that I know of, anyway.
Grand. Let me get your numbers, then I'll have a listen to your chest. ~
Go on then. ~
Pulse 74, blood pressure 126 over 78, temperature 36.5, oxygen 99 percent, and breathing 15 times a minute.
Is that all fine? You've gone quiet. ~
Sorry, I was writing. All fine, yes. Take a deep breath in for me, and out. ~
In and out. Do I need to take my top off? ~
No, over the vest is fine. Chest is clear both sides, and I can't feel any swollen glands in your neck.
Is that good? ~
It's what I'd hoped for. Because lupus and your kidneys can make your immune system weaker, the vaccines matter more for you than for most. ~
So can I have them today? ~
I'll give you the pneumonia jab today, in your arm. The flu one, we'll do when the new batch comes in next month.
And the shingles one? ~
I'd like to check your blood first, to see how your immune system is doing, before we decide on that one. I'll send a blood test for your antibody levels.
Will I get a letter? ~
You'll get the result by text within a week. And I'd like you to come back in four weeks, so we can decide on the shingles jab together.
Four weeks. I'll put it in my phone. Will the jab today make me poorly? ~
A sore arm, maybe a bit tired tomorrow. If you get a high temperature or feel really unwell, ring us.
Right you are. Thanks ever so much. ~
You're welcome. Mind how you go. ~
